clue.text: Make good mate after Rome vacation

indicators.note: the mate comes after the emptied city in the answer
a vacated place is emptied, so the word Rome loses its inside and keeps only its ends

parts.note: a mate is one of a pair, a partner

explanation.surface: Someone tells a partner to put things right after a holiday in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rome vacation' looks like a trip, but 'vacation' empties Rome to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good damage is to fix or mend it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Vocal person auctioning room

indicators.note: vocal means spoken out, so the word for the person auctioning is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: someone auctioning goods is a seller

explanation.surface: A loud auctioneer fills the sale room with their voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is an underground storage room beneath a house.

clue.text: Large dock arranged private security measure

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters of dock are reordered

parts.note: something private is your own

explanation.surface: A big dock has been set up as a private security zone.
explanation.definitionFit: A lockdown is an emergency restriction on movement, imposed for safety.

clue.text: Relieving tension, excusing mates in conflict

parts.note: excusing someone a punishment is letting them off

indicators.note: mates in conflict are thrown into disorder, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Friends at odds are forgiven, easing the strain between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting off steam is an idiom for releasing pent-up emotion or energy.

clue.text: Directors of vehicle company making relocation to North Cheam

indicators.note: relocation moves things about, so the letters of Cheam are shifted around

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: Bosses of a coach firm are moving the business to North Cheam, a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheam is a suburb in south-west London; 'relocation' shuffles it to ACHME before the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Coachmen drove horse-drawn coaches, so they directed the vehicle.

clue.text: Establish food store with German

parts.note: a deli, short for delicatessen, is a food shop
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: Someone is setting up a food shop with a German partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To delimit is to fix or settle the limits of something, so to establish its bounds.

clue.text: Still lifting item, needing energy for last of stamina

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so energy replaces the other letter

parts.note: a windlass is a winch used for hoisting loads

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A worker, still hoisting a load, needs energy to keep up their stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing energy for last of stamina' swaps the A (last of stamina) in WINDLASS for E.
explanation.definitionFit: Still air is calm, with no breeze, so the day is without wind.

clue.text: Folk exercise by pole dancing

parts.note: PE stands for physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: dancing jiggles the letters of pole into a new order

explanation.surface: Ordinary people are getting fit with a spot of pole dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Folk and people are plain synonyms for persons in general.

clue.text: Taste dish containing innards of ram

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the plate wraps round the other letter

parts.note: a plate is a dish

indicators.note: innards are the insides, so the middle letter of ram is taken

explanation.surface: Someone samples a plate of offal from a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A palate is a sense of taste, as in a refined palate for wine.

clue.text: Following guards right behind

indicators.note: guards means surrounds protectively, so the outer word wraps round the other letter

parts.note: tailing someone is following them closely

explanation.surface: A tail is shadowing someone, with bodyguards close behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner trailing in a race is lagging at the back, so behind the others.

clue.text: Be unsuccessful finding accommodation after some time in US

indicators.note: the accommodation is placed after the season

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
a flat is an apartment, a place to live

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a place to stay after a spell in America.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall flat is an idiom for failing to have the intended effect, like a joke that flops.

clue.text: I'm to reflect in religious sermon

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: holy means sacred or religious

indicators.note: reflect as in a mirror, so the letters of I'm are turned back to front

explanation.surface: A preacher is about to reflect deeply within a religious sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: A homily is a talk on a religious theme, usually by a priest.

clue.text: Losing article, suspicion about new associates

indicators.note: losing means giving up, so the article is dropped from the word

parts.note: a breath of scandal is a hint or suspicion of it
a is the indefinite article
re means about, as in business letters

explanation.surface: Someone drops a suspicion about their new colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Brethren are fellow members of a society or religious order, people associated together.

clue.text: Good nosh in excess makes you extremely big

indicators.note: in puts the eating inside the other word

parts.note: the rest is what is left over, the surplus
nosh is slang for food, and to nosh is to eat

explanation.surface: Overeating good food will make you very large indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatest is the superlative of great, so it means largest of all.

clue.text: Dishes from Verona we smashed

indicators.note: smashed means broken up, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Plates from Verona that we have broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovenware is the collective name for heatproof dishes used for baking.

clue.text: German trio ending four months on ship

parts.note: September, October, November and December all end in the same three letters
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: A German threesome finishes a four-month cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: A Berliner is a native of Berlin, so a German person.

clue.text: Left field by opening in fence on the other side

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: left over means remaining, so over can stand for left
lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A field on the left is reached through a gap in the fence on the far side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a direction (L), but here it means remaining, as in 'left over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Overleaf means on the reverse of a page, its other side.

clue.text: Ordinary metal in rake

indicators.note: in places the metal inside the other word

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man, a roue
tin is a metallic element

explanation.surface: A garden rake has a plain metal head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake' looks like the garden tool, but it is a roue, a libertine.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine as an adjective means commonplace and unremarkable.

clue.text: I agree nothing should be dropped from medieval shows

indicators.note: in a down clue, dropping a letter moves it lower down the word, here to the bottom

parts.note: jousts were knightly tournaments held in the Middle Ages
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that nothing should be cut from medieval pageants.
explanation.walkthrough: The O is not deleted but moved to the end of JOUSTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Just so is a dated phrase of assent, like exactly or quite right.

clue.text: Shabby fur: sides split

indicators.note: shabby means worn and messy, so the letters are knocked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A worn fur coat has torn at the sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Fissured means cracked open, having fissures or splits.

clue.text: Mounted soldiers hired to contain a riot

indicators.note: to contain means to hold inside, so the other letter goes within
in a down clue, mounted means raised up, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: mercs is short for mercenaries, hired soldiers

explanation.surface: Cavalry mercenaries are brought in to quell a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' suggests horsemen, but it reverses MERCS to SCREM.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hilarious is a riot or a scream: both mean very funny.

clue.text: Fabrics rejected time and again, they're not allowed back

indicators.note: rejected means thrown out, so letters are removed

parts.note: textiles are woven fabrics

indicators.note: again asks for the time letter a second time, giving two of it

explanation.surface: Cloth repeatedly turned away, never allowed back into the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Exiles are people banished from their country and barred from returning.

clue.text: A Parisian fellow with address online is open

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it
a URL is a web address

explanation.surface: A French man with a website is open to contact.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfurl a flag or sail is to unroll it, to open it out.

clue.text: Hear legend of seabird and run away

indicators.note: hear says the words are listened to, so the phrase sounds like the answer

parts.note: a tern is a seabird and a tale is a legend

explanation.surface: Listen to the old story of a seabird and then flee.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is to flee, as an animal turns to show its back.

clue.text: Courage to change sides shows inconsistency

indicators.note: sides here are left and right, so the left letter is swapped for the right one

parts.note: valiance means bravery or courage

explanation.surface: It takes courage to switch allegiance, which looks inconsistent.
explanation.definitionFit: A variance is a discrepancy or difference, so a lack of consistency.

clue.text: One flies to cave in orderly fashion

indicators.note: putting into order rearranges the letters of to cave

explanation.surface: A bat flies neatly to its cave.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a wading bird with an upturned bill, so one that flies.

clue.text: Spirit after cold beer addled part of brain

indicators.note: the spirit comes after the other pieces

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: addled means muddled, so the letters of beer are jumbled

parts.note: rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A spirit chaser after cold beer has left someone's brain fuddled.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain, its two hemispheres.
